# An unclosed formal three-cap menu, with its missing facet geometry

This is an exact scalar obstruction to declaring the joint profile and
residual-volume tests alone complete. It is NOT a convex-body construction,
not an actual critical circuit, and not a counterexample to OC.

Set d=2 and normalize whole-fiber areas to

    a=1/10, c=1, b=1, M=21/10, Gamma=4/9.

The OC raw target is T=7/15. Consider the formal common cap mass
Q=93/200<T and these arrays:

                cap 1        cap 2        cap 3
    middle q    37/100       367/800      367/800
    A mass U    19/200         1/160        1/160
    B mass V       0              0            0.

Each column sums to Q. All middle masses and A masses are proper;
U_i+V_i<=a and Q<=3q_i. The whole-fiber areas are strictly nonheavy,
and their endpoint roots satisfy sqrt(a)+sqrt(b)<2. Also
Gamma*max(a,c,b)<Q<T. These facts are necessary scalar conditions only.

The ordinary three-cap profiles hold on both the purported covered
bodies K and A. Their weighted top-three values are, respectively,

    q_2+q_3+q_1/4=101/100>=1,
    U_1+U_2+U_3/4=329/3200>=1/10.

Because 1/Gamma=9/4 lies strictly between two and three, these are the
minima over all thresholds of their ordinary distal profile functions.
Thus their full ordinary profiles, not only one arbitrarily chosen
threshold, are consistent. Consequently the joint interval-distance
profile derived from these two profiles is also consistent.

Each residual BM constraint holds. With r_i=a-U_i and t_i=1-q_i,
its form is sqrt(r_i)+1<=2sqrt(t_i). Since 4t_i-r_i-1>0, it suffices
and is equivalent to

    (4t_i-r_i-1)^2>=4r_i.

For cap 1, r_1=1/200,t_1=63/100; for caps 2 and 3,
r_i=3/32,t_i=433/800. Direct rational arithmetic certifies the displayed
inequalities. No captured-BM inequality requiring two positive captured
endpoint bodies is invoked, as every B capture is zero.

The verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_joint_profile_planar_volume_exclusion.py` checks
these statements together with the independent planar volume-tuple
exclusion. Passing them does not establish compatibility with a common
family of actual halfspaces on common convex bodies.

## The geometric condition hidden by the zero entries

If such an array came from actual depth-attaining caps, every zero B
capture would have to be a genuine supporting-facet cut. In particular,
it could not be made strictly empty by putting its boundary beyond B.
For a proper A cut, increasing the integer tilt then decreases A capture
at a strictly positive first-order rate while leaving a strictly empty
B cut empty, contradicting minimality.

The complete directional proof is in
`candidate 568f7cf028ec23b6`,
independently audited in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
For a cap normal u, let sigma_A be its actual A cutting-section length
and F_B the actual B supporting face. Then necessarily

    sigma_A<=H_1(F_B).

The full criticality condition is stronger: if c_A,c_K are the section
centroids and sigma_K the K section length, then for every continuous
perturbation w and integer perturbation beta,

    sigma_A[w.(c_A-y)-beta]+sigma_K w.(c_K-y)
       +integral_(F_B)[w.(x-y)+beta]_+ dH_1(x)>=0.

Furthermore, in a full-rank three-cap positive circuit with all B captures
zero, the same source proves that one allowed common fiber shear and
positive rescaling of the cap equations put all cuts into the form

    v_i.x>=z,  sum v_i=0,

and put the same whole B body inside the single triangle

    T={x:v_i.x<=1 for every i}.

Each of its three B cuts must touch the corresponding side in a positive
length face, and all these faces belong to that same convex body B.
The midpoint of each A section at level -1 and its B supporting face
at level +1 must lie in the K section at level zero. This does not imply
B=T, nor does it make the section lengths and centroids freely assignable.
The displayed formal volume menu has not been shown to satisfy this
shared facet geometry or the full directional criticality inequalities.
